bit.title: Prove the sharp finite-stage BIT bootstrap and the supplier thresholds required for kappa = 0.005
bit.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Prove the sharp finite-stage frontier of the completed ordinary BIT wrapper,
then work backward from kappa=1/200 to the stronger covered supplier it needs.
**No new kappa.** The selected result remains .00363005817 (#7000/#7001).

For rational 0<=b<C<1/2 and fixed stage depth h, the full three-term source
cost has one-stage supremum F_C(b)=C/(1+C-b). It is not attained under strict
slack. With y=C^h(C-b)/(1-b), the h-stage supremum is (C-y)/(1-y); the proof
gives the exact inverse target test and rational witnesses below that bound.
An acyclic portfolio using covered prices at most C cannot cross C.

From selected b=.00385248, one stage reaching .005 needs covered
C>3112961/621875000. A hypothetical C=.0050001 needs exactly two stages;
explicit rho=.0051 choices reach ordinary .00500007. The current covered
.0038525298 and atom rho=.004 cannot fund the target. This is a limitation
of the frozen cost interface, not a universal BIT lower bound.

## Full costs and target join

The bill retains e^(1-rho), e^((1-rho)(1-C)+rho(1-b)), and e^rho log(e),
all multiplied by complete volume and a fresh finite constant. Completed
predecessors, input-dependent stock depth, whole-job routing, restoration,
fixed thresholds and all spectator contracts remain required.

The hypothetical BIT output joins uniform complex .00500006 in the actual
54 strict and four functional outer checks. A separate input-lift proof
repairs the old sufficient guard through .0051. No stronger covered BIT or
complex native is constructed. This is not complete conditional .005.

## Sources and verification

Canonical base: e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57. Nine exact input
Git/SHA256 pins bind the selected review, delayed-cover proof, finite ordinary
bootstrap, current checker and Nick Petalas's prior outer-region theorem.

```sh
python3 -I -B research/bit-target-bootstrap/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/bit-target-bootstrap/independent.py
```

Both also passed with -O on authenticated source exports. Author checks cover
1,520 exact identities,18,810 full-cost comparisons and570 witnesses; the
independent matrix derivation checks450 cases and5,000 comparisons. Controls
reject zero slack, omitted adapter/stock, one-stage overclaim and unfunded BIT.
Expected markers: PASS_TARGET_BIT_BOOTSTRAP and PASS_INDEPENDENT_BOOTSTRAP_REVIEW.
The generic registry runner was not executed in this source-export environment.

## Limits and credit

All five foundational assumptions remain. No whole supplier replay, new native,
selected-frontier update, human peer review or proof-kernel acceptance is claimed.
Credit Rohan Arun's #185 lineage, BagMan9's #768 tied-depth precedent, T37,
zxv, Cinna Davis, Jacob Alan Sussman, DreamingOfClouds and the current source
authors. The decoupled atom/covered optimum differs from the prior tied affine
recurrence. Prepared for @CubeJerry with substantial OpenAI assistance; separate
model-assisted adversarial review. Apache-2.0.

owned.title: Prove the paid-rank versus scalar-work floor for all 23 selected owned rises (no new kappa)
owned.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Prove a paid-rank versus scalar-work obstruction for isolated replacements of
all 23 owned rises in selected #7000. **No new kappa.** This excludes a specific
tempting route to .005, not that target or joint rewrites generally.

Every actual rise has a nonzero coefficient of an independent public array.
Complex-array surjectivity, or spanning scaled inputs on exact grids, forces
a single-input replacement to implement the complete prescribed map.

## Exact result and target relevance

At column count f, a linear replacement with g whole-field ADDs and Gaussian
children of total rank s has row support at most 2^(g+s*f). The rank-r return
has 2^(r*f) equal-modulus entries. Squared operator error is at least
max(0,1-2^(g-(r-s)*f)); exactness or error below 1/sqrt(2) requires
g>=(r-s)*f. Arbitrary monomial maps/scalars and independent scratch are allowed;
external data-dependent side information is excluded.

At t=199/200, paid moment below r^t implies s<r, hence at least f ADDs.
Fixed native templates cannot do this for all f; literal full-field scans cost
Omega(V*f), exceeding O(V*f^t*polylog(f)). Fused/partial-field algorithms and
changed boundaries remain outside scope. The r*f-ADD butterfly is checked
as the admitted scalar escape.

The 23-rise histogram has rank mass56 per native. Removing all 18 occurrences
for free would move the actual moment from about -567.716011 to +434.821363.
The theorem blocks funding that relaxation through these isolated lower-rank
replacements. Joint correlations, changed trajectories, productive targets and
new interfaces remain possible. The selected Gaussian factorization is inherited,
not inferred from binary frame dimension alone.

## Sources and verification

Canonical base: e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57. The complete source
word and invoice have exact Git/SHA256 pins in SOURCES.json. Forward rows and
an independent reverse-prefix adjoint match all 23 pivots and support sizes 79-314.
Independent checks cover 1,095 frame bases, 71,261 events and 54 lifetimes.

```sh
python3 -I -B research/selected-owned-rank-tradeoff/verify.py
python3 -I -B research/selected-owned-rank-tradeoff/independent.py
python3 -I -B research/selected-owned-rank-tradeoff/independent_budget.py
```

Normal/-O author and independent checks passed on exact source exports.
Controls include wrong phase, omitted axis, dependent frame, altered pivot,
undercharged rise and the full-price scalar escape. Independent exact roots
confirm the target budget. Expected markers: PASS_SELECTED_OWNED_RANK_TRADEOFF,
PASS_INDEPENDENT_REVERSE_OWNED_AUDIT and PASS_INDEPENDENT_OWNED_BUDGET.
No full native catalogue cold replay or generic registry run is claimed.

## Limits and credit

All five foundational assumptions remain; no complete conditional .005 or
unconditional theorem. Credit #6914's paid owned-ascent realization,
Matarener's #5445 historical nested floor, Nick Petalas's #5111 sparse-row
approximation and #679's volume warnings, plus #7000/#7001 and their full
native/helper/compiler lineage. Classical support counting is credited.
Prepared for @CubeJerry with substantial OpenAI assistance and separate
model-assisted adversarial review. Apache-2.0; no human/kernel acceptance.

selector.title: Construct the BIT selector lift and prove its full paid repair cannot reach kappa = 0.005
selector.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Construct and price a concrete shared-core BIT attempt, then prove why its displayed repair cannot reach kappa = 1/200. **No new kappa.** Selected saving remains .00363005817 (#7000/#7001).

The division-free selector retains one helper/owned core and duplicates 222 main fields. The selected copy follows the original word; each passive difference follows its main-only M0. Authenticated replay finds M0=I, while the required endpoint contains 111 independent Y<-Y+X shears. Sharing labels leaves real work unfinished.

## Exact theorem and complete bill

For each port/passive copy, initialize zero in the full rank-8 source chart, collect the two X values, pay a nested rank-1 MOVE to the rank-7 target chart, add to Y and erase. This six-event repair preserves arbitrary inputs and adds 111(m-1) paid rank-1 jobs per native. Its normalized endpoint is correct; physical all-width admission remains inherited.

At t=199/200, let M2 be the complete current paired BIT moment and D the core paid moment minus helper credit. Exact bounds give M2<-444 and D<88. For every fixed even m>=2:

    M(m)=(m/2)M2+18(m-1)(D-111)<-222m-414(m-1)<0.

Every native, root target, query and idle is retained; lost helper copies are debited. This excludes this literal lift-plus-repair family's moment gate, not cheaper repairs or shared cores generally. Omitting the repair charge produces a false positive.

The native has 222m+437 public fields, 238 owned labels and 34137+23620(m-1) events. Initialization, gathering, MOVEs and erasure are counted. The recursive moment fails even with new ordinary work free. No old scalar, precision, storage or tape constant transfers.

## Sources and independent verification

Canonical base: e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57. Native blob b718d6b2848215ad785022106dfa9f871a3d1c0c and raw caller cf55f4271009a06ad192a070d330a4466b6d44fa are frozen with SHA256 guards and notices. SOURCES.json pins caller proof and native conventions.

```sh
node research/bit-selector-lift-price/verify.js
python3 -I -B research/bit-selector-lift-price/review/independent.py --word research/bit-selector-lift-price/inputs/native.json.gz --caller research/bit-selector-lift-price/inputs/query_only_6980.json
```

Node and normal/-O independent Python passed. Independent reverse adjoints and rational log/exp bounds differ from the author's forward rows and integer roots. Checks cover 636 rational frames, all 659 original endpoint columns, repaired m=2,4,6 endpoints, actual chart/lifetime rules and literal root-caller recount. Controls reject source mutation, missing repair, free cross-chart ADD and omitted paid repair. Markers: PASS_BIT_SELECTOR_LIFT_PAID_REPAIR and PASS_INDEPENDENT_REVERSE_SELECTOR_LIFT. No generic registry run is claimed.

## Limits and credit

All five assumptions remain, including nonzero owned erasure. No complete conditional .005, unconditional theorem or selected update. Different sharing, cheaper corrections and new interfaces remain open. #7146/#7149 concern retained-summary descent covers; this result concerns whole-main replication with one complete core. Credit DreamingOfClouds, zxv, @CubeJerry and retained native/caller authors and notices. Prepared for @CubeJerry with substantial OpenAI assistance and separate model-assisted review. Apache-2.0; no human or kernel review.

fragmentation.title: Prove the kappa = 0.005 helper-refinement barrier, sharp 1,276-extra-target threshold and paid compiler specification
fragmentation.body:
## Change and mathematical scope

**No new κ.** Starting from selected conditional κ=363005817/100000000000 at canonical main `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`, this package derives the helper refinement required at κ★=1/200, proves a sharp obstruction and threshold, and checks a downstream compiler specification. It does not turn a partition inventory into a physical supplier.

The #7000/#7001 invoice retains all 117,612 paid positions and 3,952 root targets. Every replaced helper credit is debited; old and new credits are never counted together.

## Exact result

1. Partitions of each selected original helper into **at most two positive integer descendants** fail the raw moment for every C in [1/200,1). Concavity and 24 exact integer-product/Abel inequalities prove this continuum theorem.
2. Even granting free implementation and arbitrary partitions, the sharp threshold is **22,954 extra caller targets**; 22,953 fails. Repeating one native 18 times requires **1,276 extras per native**; 1,275 fails. The attaining profile {1:13,2:18,3:1808,4:408,5:109} includes 554 rank-nine helpers split as 3+3+3.
3. All 4,657 existing-chart 3/6 first-cut classes in the unchanged source are excluded: 4,496 lack a pure prefix image, 136 a pure suffix image, and 25 have zero full-kernel pairing. This blocks only the specified source-fixed sequential ternary route.
4. **Conditional on an unbuilt native exposing that profile**, a paid compiler specification at C=.00500007 uses product power 1920, paid cap 11^1920, target floor 12^1920 and actual ambient 153^1920. The complete paid-plus-discarded-target bound is below .999. Honest logarithmic exponent 1377 and an explicit finite threshold yield uniform U=.00500006.

The compiler retains every intermediate paid call and counts discarded inputs as owned storage with initialization/erasure and new finite constants. A separately verified BIT bridge shows that an **unbuilt** covered supplier at .0050001 gives ordinary B=.00500007 in two stages, compatible with the current 54+4 outer rows. Neither supplier is constructed: this is not a complete conditional κ=.005 result.

## Sources and verification

Word Git blob: `74563a7867d9d762b6588f65362369668841bb3e`; full invoice: `ff3256f0d3ffbfc56b062f9ec0fdbbc7b30e76d5`. Both are pinned to the canonical base. SOURCES.json records exact input/dependency hashes.

```sh
python -I -B research/moonshot-helper-fragmentation/verify.py
python -I -B research/moonshot-helper-fragmentation/static_cut.py
python -I -B research/moonshot-helper-fragmentation/compiler_certificate.py
```

Expected markers: PASS_SHARP_HELPER_FRAGMENTATION, PASS_STATIC_3_6_CUT_OBSTRUCTION, PASS_UNBUILT_PROFILE_COMPILER_SPECIFICATION. All eight registered command groups completed, covering twelve author/reviewer normal/optimized replays. Independent methods use a partition dual, a different full-kernel construction and separate rational log/exp bounds. Controls cover duplicate credit, missing paid work, source corruption, invalid offsets, false ambient and adjacent failing thresholds. Retained runner schema validation passed; full Git-backed registry execution, hosted CI and formal-kernel acceptance are not claimed.

## Limits and credit

All five canonical assumptions remain: native_all_columns, owned_erasure, compiler, precision_tape, analytic_recovery. Physical suppliers, current ownership, actual ordinary tariffs, precision and uniform contracts remain required. The finite census excludes its specified cuts, not every ternary architecture.

Prepared for **@CubeJerry** with substantial **OpenAI Codex assistance**, including separate research and adversarial-review agents. Credit DreamingOfClouds' native lineage, Ali Romman's split criterion, Matarener's earlier census, Nick Petalas's balancing/exact-root precedent and retained #6916/#6912/#6914/#6930/#7000 contributors. Higher-moment, target-restriction and ambient-cap methods retain predecessor credit.
